did_you_know.text: Did you know? Job responds to his friends sarcastically: they are not the only ones who have wisdom, and he claims that he too has understanding and insight.
Did you know? Job describes a painful moral reversal: the sufferer becomes an object of ridicule, even though those who live at ease may be people who provoke God.
Did you know? To learn about God’s ways, Job directs his friends to the natural world: the animals, the birds, the earth, and the fish of the sea.
Did you know? Job declares that all creation testifies to the work of the LORD: “The hand of the LORD has done this.”
Did you know? According to Job, God holds in his hand the life of every living creature and the spirit of every human being; life itself depends on him.
Did you know? Job uses the senses of taste and hearing as an image of discernment: the ear tests words just as the palate tastes food.
Did you know? The chapter brings together God’s attributes—wisdom, power, counsel, and understanding—and presents them as the source of his control over reality.
Did you know? Job emphasizes that human beings cannot undo God’s works: if God tears down or shuts, no one can rebuild or open by their own power.
Did you know? God’s rule includes those in positions of authority: he leads counselors away as captives and confuses the judgment of judges.

Did you know? At the end of the passage, God is described as revealing deep things from darkness, but he can also take understanding away from the leaders of nations and leave them groping in the darkness.
